title: Frontend: groupBy(arr, key)
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind groupBy(arr, key). This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({records,key}). Group records by String(record[key]) and return ordered [key,records] pairs, preserving first-seen bucket order and record order. Missing keys become undefined. Prototype-looking keys must work.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Use a Map when keys may be objects or when arbitrary string keys must not collide with object prototypes.
alternativeApproaches: Accept a key-selector function and compare Map identity semantics with serialized compound keys.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Empty array; missing key; __proto__ string.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
